answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks: transition mass reaching a candidate is damped at each step, while normalization limits influence. A sybil cluster forms a sparse external cut with low conductance φ, so few walks escape its boundary; Cheeger-style bounds constrain its stationary mass and therefore its aggregate voting weight. Honest attestations may whisper through an oasis, but cannot let identities wander unchecked across the cut.
